findings.title: FINAL_LOWER uses the lower of the cash and card totals, so a cash-to-card tender swap is never flagged
findings.scenario: Lines 735-736 and 792 compare the final total with min(totalCents, cardTotalCents) instead of the pre-bill total for the tender actually used. Example: a cash pre-bill for Smash shows PKR 1,150 cash (15% GST) and PKR 1,080 if paid by card (8%). The guest pays the cashier PKR 1,150 in cash. The cashier records a manual-reference 'card' tender, so processPayment re-prices the order to the card rate and it completes at 1,080. The cashier keeps PKR 70. finalTotalCents 108000 equals lowestShown, so the row gets no FINAL_LOWER flag, 'Flagged only' hides it, and summary.finalLower leaves it out. The table still shows a red −70 difference that nothing flags. This skim is the case FINAL_LOWER exists to catch. Spec §17.3 says to compare against totalCents, and the builder's deviation #1 removes that control instead of narrowing it.
findings.fix: Compare against the pre-bill total for the tender the order was actually settled with. In listPreBills, also load `payments: { where: { status: 'paid', amountCents: { gt: 0 } }, select: { method: true } }` for the orders. If every paid tender is card or keenu_qr, use base = p.cardTotalCents ?? p.totalCents. Otherwise, when any cash was paid, use base = (p.tender === 'cash' ? p.totalCents : the cash total). Then finalLower = converted && finalTotalCents < base. Use the same base for summary.finalLower.diffCents. Add a test: a cash pre-bill whose order is settled as cash but completed at the card total must be flagged.

findings.title: Summary counts every reprint, so orphaned, line-void and printed amounts are multiplied
findings.scenario: Lines 732-741 flag each PreBill row on its own, and lines 787-795 add each flagged row's cents into the summary. markPreBillsCancelledTx moves open AND superseded rows to cancelled, and the 12 h and closed-drawer rules also apply to superseded rows. Example: a waiter prints a PKR 5,000 pre-bill three times for one table, then a manager cancels the order. The Orphaned tile shows 3 / PKR 15,000 although PKR 5,000 walked. Likewise, if one PKR 400 line is voided after three prints, lineVoidsAfter shows 3 / PKR 1,200. The 'Pre-bills printed' value also triples. Finance reads these tiles as leakage, so the exposure is overstated by the number of reprints.
findings.fix: Keep the per-row flags, since every print is a permanent record, but count the summary money once per order. Group the rows by orderId and take the highest-numbered row per order for orphaned.cents, lineVoidsAfter.cents (voids are per order) and valueCents. Alternatively, report both prints and orders, e.g. orphaned { count, orders, cents }. Add a test with an order printed twice and then cancelled: orphaned.cents must equal one total.

findings.title: markPreBillsCancelledTx does not lock the order, so a concurrent print can leave an 'open' pre-bill on a cancelled order with no manager recorded
findings.scenario: createPreBill holds the order row FOR UPDATE while it supersedes old rows and inserts a new one. The hook (lines 388-400) only runs updateMany on pre_bills. Today's cancel path (orders/service.ts ~L998) is a bare order.updateMany with no order lock. If W4 calls the hook before its order write, the following can happen. T1 (print) locks the order and supersedes PB-7. T2 (cancel) runs the hook, blocks on PB-7's row lock, and starts its statement snapshot. T1 inserts PB-8 'open' and commits. T2's updateMany re-checks PB-7, cancels it, never sees PB-8, and then cancels the order. Result: PB-8 stays 'open' on a cancelled order with cancelledById and cancelReason null, so the Voided pre bills drawer shows no 'Cancelled' section and no approving manager for the last bill the guest saw. In the reverse order the two transactions deadlock and the cancel fails with a 500.
findings.fix: Make both hooks self-serialising. Call `await lockOrderTx(tx, orderId)` at the top of markPreBillsCancelledTx and markPreBillsConvertedTx (a re-lock in the same transaction is a no-op). Alternatively, state in the hook's doc comment and in needsOtherFiles that W4 must lock or update the order row before calling it. Optionally have listPreBills treat an 'open' row whose order is cancelled or rejected as cancelled for display.

findings.title: A pre-bill for a part-paid order prints the whole bill as TOTAL with no amount paid or balance due
findings.scenario: createPreBill refuses only fully paid orders (line 194), so a pre-bill can be printed on a part-paid order. The quote's paidCents and dueCents are discarded, and receiptOf and renderPreBillHtml print only 'TOTAL (CASH) PKR X'. Example: a table of four splits a PKR 10,000 bill and two guests pay PKR 5,000 by card. A pre-bill printed for the rest shows TOTAL PKR 10,000 and nothing about the PKR 5,000 already paid. The guest is shown, and may hand over, twice what is due. The FnF receipt (pos/receipt.ts) prints the payments, but the pre-bill, the only bill now allowed for an open order (§17.1 PRE_BILL_REQUIRED), does not.
findings.fix: Return quote.paidCents and quote.dueCents on PreBillReceipt and print 'Paid so far' and 'Balance due' lines in renderPreBillHtml when paidCents > 0. For later re-renders without a schema change, rebuild them from the order's paid payments with processedAt/createdAt <= preBill.printedAt. Alternatively, ask W0 to add PreBill.paidCents. Add a test: part-pay an order, print a pre-bill, and assert the receipt's dueCents equals the quote's dueCents.
